claims.text: The target alloy is an equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy.
WTaTiVZr consists of reduced- or low-activation refractory elements suitable for nuclear service.
The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy has a homogeneous BCC or simple solid-solution microstructure.
Powder metallurgy followed by spark plasma sintering can be used to synthesize the target alloy.
Equimolar mixing in WTaTiVZr produces severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion creates a heterogeneous internal stress field.
The distortion-induced stress field facilitates activation of multiple slip systems.
The distortion-induced stress field supports dynamic dislocation recovery, including cross-slip and rearrangement.
Time-dependent deformation of TaTiVWZr can be dislocation dominated, with thermally activated dislocations contributing as temperature increases.
Large local lattice strains enhance dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr.
Enhanced cross-slip and dynamic recovery prevent localized dislocation pile-up.
Multiple slip and recovery homogenize plastic flow and delay strain localization and crack nucleation.
Under identical high-temperature sustained loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature sustained loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater toughness, work to failure, or delayed crack propagation relative to pure tungsten.

Commercially pure tungsten has limited plastic deformation and lower toughness under the proposed high-temperature loading because of brittle behavior and a high ductile-to-brittle transition temperature.
The proposed mechanism applies around or above 1000 degrees Celsius under sustained or cyclic loading where rate-dependent dislocation processes are active.
Matching processing history, geometry, grain-size scale, stress state, and temperature between WTaTiVZr and tungsten is intended to isolate the effect attributed to alloying and lattice distortion.
Plastic strain, work of fracture or crack-onset behavior, dislocation structures, slip-system activation, and recovery signatures can be measured in the controlled comparison.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in both plastic strain and toughness, or failure to observe more homogeneous dislocation activity and dynamic recovery, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
The quantitative improvements and the relative contributions of recovery, slip activation, and grain-boundary effects are presently uncertain.
